title: Rerank onboarding checklist and mini-audit
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic checklist and mini-audit to use during model onboarding for reranker-style evaluations. It captures the minimal set of checks, sampling rules, and sanity calculations we run before accepting a new model into staging/dedicated deployment. Use this as a quick gate before full-scale pairwise annotation or NDCG evaluation.

Scope and assumptions:
- Focus: reranker outputs (top-K lists) for retrieval + candidate scoring stacks.
- Labels we gather: pairwise preference (A preferred / B preferred / tie).
- Downstream metric: NDCG@10 (and NDCG@3 for latency-sensitive flows).
- This is NOT the full experiment spec — it is a quick operational guide for the first pass audit.

Checklist (pre-annotation):
1) Sampling sanity
   - Confirm dataset provenance: query log slice, synthetic prompts, or curated eval set. Add source tag.
   - Ensure deduping at query level and candidate level for the batch. No identical candidates across pair rounds.
   - Sample sizes: aim for at least 1,200 pairwise judgments (rough guide) distributed across slices; for tiny pilots 300 pairs OK.
   - Balanced sampling across slices (see slice definitions).

2) Pair construction rules
   - Only compare candidate pairs that were produced within the same top-K for a given query (prevent cross-query comparisons).
   - Include reverse pairs (A vs B and B vs A) for 5% of items as a consistency check.
   - Insert 5% golden pairs (previously annotated high-confidence pairs) to measure annotator drift.

3) Annotator instructions (short):
   - Task: "Which answer would you prefer to show a real user for this query?"
   - Accept partial information: prefer on relevance and helpfulness, not style unless asked.
   - Tie is allowed when neither candidate is clearly better.
   - Flag hallucinations or safety issues with tags.

4) Quick QA scripts to run before sending to annotators
   - Reverse-pair agreement check (expect >95% internal consistency on synthetic reversals).
   - Duplicate prompt/candidate detection; fail if >2% duplicates.
   - Length distribution check vs production baseline (mean and median token lengths).

Mini-audit: lightweight metrics we compute immediately after first 100 annotations
- Pair preference distribution: percent A wins / B wins / ties. Expect neither model to exceed 70% wins unless the difference is large.
- Annotator agreement: compute pairwise Cohen's kappa across annotators on overlapping pairs. Flag if kappa < 0.30 (low).
- Golden pair accuracy: fraction of golden items labeled correctly; flag if <90%.

Converting pairwise labels into ranking metrics (practical recipe)
- For each query construct a preference graph where nodes are candidate IDs and directed edges indicate preference counts.
- Convert to a per-query ranking score via Borda-style aggregation: score(candidate) = sum over opponents of wins(candidate,opponent). 
- Produce a ranked list per query by descending score.
- Compute NDCG@K using those reconstructed ranks against the reference relevance derived from majority votes or expert labels.

NDCG quick example (walkthrough)
- Query q1 has 3 candidates: c1, c2, c3. Pair labels: c1>c2, c1>c3, c2>c3.
  - Borda scores: c1=2, c2=1, c3=0 => ranking c1, c2, c3.
  - Assume relevance labels (expert): rel(c1)=3, rel(c2)=2, rel(c3)=0 (graded).
  - DCG@3 = rel(c1)/log2(1+1) + rel(c2)/log2(2+1) + rel(c3)/log2(3+1) = 3/1 + 2/1.585 + 0 = 3 + 1.261 = 4.261
  - IDCG@3 (ideal) with same relevances sorted = same 4.261 so NDCG@3 = 1.0 (sanity).
- Edge case: when only pairwise binary preferences exist and graded relevances are not available, use majority-wins ordering as proxy for relevance. Document this approximation in the final report.

Slice definitions (recommended for this mini-audit)
- HEAD: frequent, unambiguous queries (top 20% of query freq).
- TAIL: low-frequency/long-tail queries (bottom 50%).
- AMBIGUOUS: queries with multiple intent clusters (detected via clustering or manual heuristics).
- ECOMMERCE: explicit product/buying intent queries.
- LONG_FORM: queries expecting paragraph answers (avg candidate tokens > 80).

Per-slice checks (run automatically where possible)
- NDCG by slice (NDCG@3 and @10) and delta vs baseline model. Flag slices with >2 points drop in NDCG@10.
- Preference entropy per slice (if one model dominates preferences entropy low -> potential overfitting).
- Safety flags density (proportion of candidates flagged for hallucination or safety) by slice.

Regression report template (one-paragraph summary + bullet items)
- Executive summary sentence: e.g., "Model X on rerank pilot shows +1.7 NDCG@10 overall vs baseline; regression of -3.4 on AMBIGUOUS slice triggered follow-up."
- Key metrics: overall NDCG@3, NDCG@10, pairwise win-rate, annotator kappa, golden accuracy.
- Top 3 regressions by slice (slice name, NDCG delta, candidate examples).
- Top 3 improvements by slice.
- Action items: labeling expansion, model architecture hypothesis, prompt/template tweaks, follow-up A/B test plan.

Automated sanity checks (post-run) to include in CI pipeline:
1) Repro-check: rerun Borda conversion twice on same pair data -> identical ranks.
2) Stability: sample bootstrap of queries and recompute NDCG variance; fail if variance > threshold (configurable).
3) Annotator consistency: kappa under threshold creates a mandatory annotator refresher.

Open questions / decisions to make for full-scale eval:
- Should we use Borda vs Bradley-Terry or TrueSkill for converting pairwise labels? (BT gives probabilistic strengths but is heavier compute-wise).
- How many golden pairs are enough per annotator in noisy verticals?
- When to upgrade tie votes into graded relevances for NDCG?

Quick TODOs before next onboarding run:
- [ ] Add reverse-pair generation to sampling script (Liam).
- [ ] Create 100 golden pairs for ECOMMERCE slice (Priya).
- [ ] Hook kappa and golden checks into evaluation CI (Derek).
- [ ] Draft a short explainer for Product on why pairwise->NDCG conversion is an approximation (Sofia).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the initial pilot small and iterate; lots of headaches come from poor sampling rather than model differences.
- If a slice shows large regressions, run targeted pair collection just for that slice with expert annotators.
- Remember to log model seed and decoding details with the annotation batch metadata.

Appendix: useful command snippets
- reverse pair detection (pseudo): grep -E "idA,idB" pairs.csv | join - reverse_pairs.csv
- quick Borda script (pythonic): for q in queries: for c in candidates[q]: score[c]+=wins[c] ; rank=sorted(score)

End of doc.
